slides.texte_overlay:
Small habits that make
people think you're smart
Pause before you answer. Two seconds of thought makes your reply sound considered instead of rushed. Silence is fine.
Use simple words for complex ideas. Explaining clearly is a sign of deep understanding. Big words often hide confusion.
Ask follow-up questions. "And what happened next?" Curiosity shows an active mind and keeps people talking. Be curious.
Admit what you don't know. "I'm not sure, but I'd love to learn." Honesty makes everything else you say more credible.
Feed your knowledge daily. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have a fact or story to add.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have a fact or story to add.

slides.texte_overlay: Read real books, not just headlines. Deep reading gives you context that makes your opinions stronger. Read daily.
Listen more than you talk. Smart people collect ideas from others before sharing their own. Listen first, then speak with something real to add.
